correctness.rationale: Canonical RGS recurrence exhausts all 203 sources and 52 outputs at six points; an independent set-block recursion and inverse insertion verify incidence. The exact clique search with inductively valid greedy-color pruning returns maximum 14 after 452972 recursive calls. An explicit 14-source code has disjoint shadows. Exact integer certificates provide a 41-supported fractional packing of 972/64 (>15) and a length-five dual cover 25/4 (<7); size-four cover and receiver counts prove earlier equality. Full checker replay returns VERIFY_OK. No unproved generalization is used.

originality.rationale: The three inspected primary works treat ordinary symbol-preserving deletion codes, general hypergraph bounds, and RGF pattern statistics. None of their checked statements supplies the six-point set-partition deletion maximum 14 or a fractional feasible packing exceeding 15. The closest same-source partition-deletion coincidence result controls distinct outputs of one partition, not simultaneous source packings. Actual targeted source/index searches found no dominating claim; this is a qualified historical assessment with residual unindexed-source risk.

value.rationale: The canonical Bell family is a natural source for unknown single-element loss with block labels unobserved. The exact zero-error capacity at six is a natural finite invariant, and it is the first nontrivial integer-rounding failure of the standard deletion-hypergraph fractional relaxation in this channel. A disjoint source code, rational witness and reproducible upper certificate give substantive coding-theoretic value beyond table recomputation.
